label: Clear puppet filter
summary: An action of the interaction menu window that, going by its name, clears the puppet filter.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the interaction menu. The game does not say what a puppet filter is beyond the name.

label: Clear puppet preview
summary: An action of the interaction menu window that, going by its name, clears the puppet preview.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Close menu
summary: Closes the interaction menu window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of a button in that window. Other window types have a Close function of the same name.

label: Actions for puppet type
summary: A whole number: going by its name, how many actions are available for the given puppet type.
details: Vanilla passes it the puppet type of the current entry of the puppet filter and shows the result as text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The puppet type to count for.
fields.values: a puppet type, for example PuppetInteractionsFilter.GetPuppetType

label: Available puppets
summary: The list of puppets the interaction menu offers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in the window, and shows that list only when it is not empty. The game does not explain what a puppet is; going by the name these are characters you can act through.

label: Category items
summary: The list of interaction categories the interaction menu shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in the window. What exactly an item holds is not stated; this rests on the name and that single use.

label: Menu character
summary: The character the interaction menu window is open for.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of the window, and a tooltip takes the character's name from it when that character is outside the diplomatic range.

label: Current puppet
summary: The puppet character currently chosen in the interaction menu.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of a part of the window. Going by its name; the game gives no further description.

label: Filter description
summary: The text that describes the filter currently applied in the interaction menu.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the window. IsFiltered is a separate function of the same window that returns a yes/no value.

label: More interactions
summary: The list of extra interactions of the interaction menu.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in the window. Going by its name; the game does not say which interactions count as more.

label: Selected puppet type
summary: The puppet type currently selected in the interaction menu.
details: Vanilla compares it with the puppet type of each entry of the puppet filter, to show or style the entry that is selected, and only while the puppet view is active.

label: Go to character
summary: An action of the interaction menu window that, going by its name, jumps to the character.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Is filtered
summary: Whether a filter is applied in the interaction menu.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether a part of the window is visible.

label: Puppet view active
summary: Whether the interaction menu is showing its puppet view.
details: Vanilla combines it with a check of the selected puppet type to show or style puppet entries, so those only react while the puppet view is on.

label: Outside diplomatic range
summary: Whether the character of the menu is outside the player's diplomatic range.
details: Vanilla shows a part of the window when it is true, and sets a margin from it (0 when true outside debug mode, otherwise 8). A tooltip text of the game says most interactions cannot be used when the character is out of range.

label: Preview puppet interactions
summary: An action of the interaction menu window that, going by its name, previews the interactions of a puppet.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; by the name, the puppet or puppet type to preview.

label: Select puppet
summary: Makes the given puppet type the selected one in the interaction menu.
details: Vanilla runs it when an entry of the puppet filter is clicked, passing that entry's puppet type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The puppet type to select.
fields.values: a puppet type, for example PuppetInteractionsFilter.GetPuppetType

label: Self
summary: The interaction menu window itself, as a value that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' Self is passed as an argument elsewhere in the game's texts; no line uses this one.

label: Accept
summary: Accepts the interaction the notification window is about.
details: Vanilla runs it from the accept button of the call-ally, interfere-in-war and marriage notification windows.

label: Access self
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the notification window itself.
details: No line uses it for this type, and the game documents nothing more. Other types have a function of the same name.

label: Acknowledge
summary: Acknowledges the interaction notification.
details: Vanilla runs it from the button of the general interaction notification window, whose text comes from GetAnswerAcknowledgeText.

label: Block
summary: Blocks the interaction the notification is about.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button of the general interaction notification window. Whether it can be used is told by CanBeBlocked.

label: Can accept
summary: Whether the notification can be accepted right now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the accept button of the call-ally, interfere-in-war and marriage notification windows.

label: Can be blocked
summary: Whether the interaction can be blocked at this moment.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable a part of the general notification window; the block button runs Block. CanPotentiallyBeBlocked is a separate function that vanilla uses for visibility.

label: Could be blocked
summary: Going by its name, whether the interaction could be blocked at all.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether a part of the general notification window is visible. CanBeBlocked is the one used to enable a part.

label: Can reject
summary: Whether the notification can be rejected right now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the reject button of the call-ally, interfere-in-war and marriage notification windows.

label: Close notification
summary: Closes the interaction notification window.
details: Vanilla runs it from close buttons of the interfere-in-war, marriage and general notification windows.

label: Accept button text
summary: The text for the accept answer of the notification.
details: Vanilla shows it as the label of the accept button in the call-ally, interfere-in-war and marriage notification windows.

label: Acknowledge button text
summary: The text for the acknowledge answer of the notification.
details: Vanilla shows it as the label of the acknowledge button in the general interaction notification window.

label: Block button text
summary: The text for the block answer of the notification.
details: Vanilla shows it as the label of the block button in the general interaction notification window.

label: Reject button text
summary: The text for the reject answer of the notification.
details: Vanilla shows it as the label of the reject button in the call-ally, interfere-in-war and marriage notification windows.

label: Block tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about whether, and why or why not, the interaction can be blocked.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of the block button. Going by the name, it explains the state that CanBeBlocked reports.

label: Interaction
summary: The character interaction the notification is about.
details: Vanilla reads ShowEffectsInNotification from it to decide whether a part of the notification windows is visible; going by that name, it is the list of effects.

label: Context name
summary: A text naming the context of the notification, shown as a text in the notification window.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the call-ally, interfere-in-war and marriage notification windows. The game does not say more about what the name is; going by the name and use it is a title-like text.

label: Effects description
summary: Going by its name, the description of the effects of the interaction.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of a part of the call-ally, interfere-in-war and general notification windows. The game does not describe what it holds.

label: Notification text
summary: The text of the interaction notification.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the shared interaction templates.

label: Sender
summary: The character who sent the interaction the notification is about.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of a part of the shared interaction templates, next to the signature texts. Going by the name and that use.

label: Signature
summary: The signature text of the interaction notification.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the shared interaction templates. GetSigned is another text used there.

label: Signed text
summary: The text that goes with the signature of the interaction notification.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the shared interaction templates. The game does not describe it further; going by the name it is the signed-by text.

label: Is auto-accepted
summary: Whether the notification is one that is accepted automatically.
details: Vanilla shows one part of the notification window when it is true and another part when it is not.

label: Reject
summary: Rejects the interaction the notification is about.
details: Vanilla runs it from the reject button of the call-ally, interfere-in-war and marriage notification windows.

label: Self
summary: The notification window itself, as a value that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' Self is passed as an argument in the game's texts; no line uses this one.

label: Access self
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the character item itself.
details: No line uses it for this type, and the game documents nothing more. Other types have a function of the same name.

label: Ally count
summary: A whole number: how many allies the character of this list entry has.
details: Vanilla shows it in the declare-war window as the number in the Allies label, and enables a part of the window only when it is above 0.

label: Character
summary: The character this entry stands for.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of a part of the declare-war window, so the parts inside can read that character's data.

label: Composition
summary: Going by its name and use, the military composition (soldiers and their quality) of this entry's character.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of a soldiers-and-quality display block, for the attacker and the defender, in the declare-war window. The game does not say what it holds beyond that.

label: Gold
summary: The gold of the character of this entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as a rounded number in the declare-war window, and checks whether it is below zero or not to show different parts.

label: Self
summary: This character item itself, handed to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the declare-war window's function that shows the allies for this character.

label: Access self
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the lifestyle window itself.
details: No line uses it for this type, and the game documents nothing more. Other types have a function of the same name.

label: Can refund perks
summary: Whether the character's perks can be reset (refunded) now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the reset button of the lifestyle window.

label: Refund perks text
summary: A text about whether the perks can be reset, and why or why not.
details: Vanilla puts it into the tooltip of the Reset Perks button, above the text about the effects of resetting.

label: Can select focus
summary: Whether the given focus can be chosen by the character.
details: Vanilla enables a focus button when this is true or the focus is already the character's current one, and shows another part when it is neither.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The focus to check.
fields.values: a focus type, for example FocusType.Self

label: Select focus text
summary: A text about whether the given focus can be chosen, and why or why not.
details: Vanilla puts it into the tooltip of a focus, between the focus name and its effect description.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The focus to explain.
fields.values: a focus type, for example FocusType.Self

label: Can select perk
summary: Whether the given perk can be unlocked now.
details: Vanilla uses it, together with a check that the character has a valid lifestyle, to enable or show the perk's select button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The perk to check.

label: Select perk text
summary: A text about whether the given perk can be unlocked, and why or why not.
details: Vanilla puts it into the perk tooltip, before the Click to unlock line, and into a shared tooltip file.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The perk to explain.

label: Can select perk ignoring cost
summary: Whether the given perk could be unlocked if its cost is left out of the check.
details: Vanilla uses it with a check that the perk is not yet unlocked, to decide which lines between perks in the perk tree are shown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The perk to check.
fields.values: a perk, for example the item at the end of a perk connection

label: Close lifestyle window
summary: Closes the lifestyle window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the close buttons of the lifestyle window.

label: Lifestyle character
summary: The character whose lifestyles the window shows.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of the lifestyle window, so everything inside reads that character.

label: Focuses
summary: The list of focuses the lifestyle window offers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in the window. Going by the name and that single use.

label: Lifestyle progress tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the progress of a lifestyle.
details: Vanilla appends it to the lifestyle experience tooltip, after the experience and experience-per-level line, passing the lifestyle.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The lifestyle the tooltip is for.

label: Lifestyles
summary: The list of lifestyles the lifestyle window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of lists in the window.

label: Perk trees
summary: The list of perk trees of the lifestyle window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in the window. Going by the name and that single use.

label: Selected focus
summary: Going by its name, the focus selected in the lifestyle window.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Selected lifestyle
summary: The lifestyle currently selected in the lifestyle window.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of a part of the window, and compares its key with a list entry's key to tell which entry is not the selected one.

label: Open focus
summary: An action of the lifestyle window that, going by its name, opens the given focus.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; by the name, the focus to open.

label: Open lifestyle
summary: Opens the given lifestyle in the lifestyle window.
details: Vanilla runs it when a lifestyle entry is clicked, passing that lifestyle.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The lifestyle to open.

label: Open perk reset
summary: Starts the reset (refund) of the character's perks from the lifestyle window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the Reset Perks button. The game does not say whether it asks for confirmation first.

label: Refund perks effects text
summary: A text describing the effects of resetting the perks.
details: Vanilla puts it into the tooltip of the Reset Perks button, after the text about whether the reset is possible.

label: Select focus
summary: Makes the given focus the character's focus.
details: Vanilla runs it when a focus is clicked in the lifestyle window. Whether it may be chosen is told by CanSelectFocus.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The focus to choose.
fields.values: a focus type, for example FocusType.Self

label: Select perk
summary: Unlocks the given perk for the character.
details: Vanilla runs it when a perk is clicked in the lifestyle window. Whether it may be unlocked is told by CanSelectPerk.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The perk to unlock.

label: Self
summary: The lifestyle window itself, as a value that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' Self is passed as an argument in the game's texts; no line uses this one.

label: Access self
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the character list filter itself.
details: No line uses it for this type, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Current filter index
summary: A pair of whole numbers saying which filter is currently chosen in the character list filter.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of a dropdown in the character filter window. The pair holds two numbers; going by the grouped filters (categories and options), they probably locate the entry in two levels, which the game does not confirm.

label: Filter name
summary: The name of the character list filter.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the character filter window.

label: Filter options
summary: The list of options the character list filter offers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in the character filter window.

label: Self
summary: The character list filter itself, as a value that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' Self is passed as an argument in the game's texts; no line uses this one.

label: Set filter from index
summary: Makes the chosen entry of the dropdown the current filter.
details: Vanilla runs it when the selection of the filter dropdown changes.

label: Access self
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the filter category itself.
details: No line uses it for this type, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Category filters
summary: Going by its name, the filters that belong to this category.
details: No line uses it for this type. A grouped filter list elsewhere in the GUI uses a GetFilters of its own, which is only a hint.

label: Category label
summary: The label text of the filter category.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the character filter window.

label: Category name
summary: The name of the filter category.
details: No line uses it for this type; going by the name, as the same function name gives names for many other types. GetLabel is the one vanilla shows.

label: Is expanded
summary: Whether the filter category is opened up to show its options.
details: Vanilla uses it to switch the frame (picture state) of the category header and to show the option list only when it is open.

label: Expand category
summary: Going by its name, the action run when the filter category is expanded.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click on a category header. Whether it toggles or only opens is not shown.

label: Self
summary: The filter category itself, as a value that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' Self is passed as an argument in the game's texts; no line uses this one.

label: Access self
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the filter option itself.
details: No line uses it for this type, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Option description
summary: The description text of a filter option.
details: Vanilla shows it as the tooltip of an option in the character filter window, under the option's name.

label: Option name
summary: The name of a filter option.
details: Vanilla shows it as the option's text, and as the heading of its tooltip.

label: Is selected
summary: Going by its name, whether the filter option is the selected one.
details: No line uses it for this type. Other types have an IsSelected of their own, which is only a hint.

label: Option click
summary: Going by its name, the action run when the filter option is clicked.
details: No line uses it for this type. Other types have an OnClick of their own, which is only a hint.

label: Self
summary: The filter option itself, as a value that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' Self is passed as an argument in the game's texts; no line uses this one.

label: Access self
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the character list entry itself.
details: No line uses it for this type, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Named yes/no value
summary: A yes/no value that the list stored for this entry under the given name.
details: Vanilla asks for can_swap in the council candidate window. Which names exist depends on the list that built the entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the stored value.

label: Entry character
summary: The character this list entry stands for.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of a part of list windows, and reads values like IsGuest from it.

label: Diplomacy skill
summary: Going by its name, the diplomacy skill of the entry's character.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it. A neighbouring function, GetMartialSkill, is used with a frame (picture state), so these likely give a skill item rather than a plain number.

label: First claim
summary: The first claim the entry's character has.
details: Vanilla makes it the context of a part of the migration, travel planner and war overview windows. Going by the name and those uses.

label: First title item
summary: Going by its name, the first title entry of the list entry.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Named decimal value
summary: A decimal number that the list stored for this entry under the given name.
details: Vanilla asks for succession_score in the diarchy window. Which names exist depends on the list that built the entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the stored value.

label: Entry index
summary: A whole number: the position of this entry in its list.
details: Vanilla hands it to other functions to find the matching data for the entry, for example a score of a merit pool. Whether counting starts at 0 is not shown.

label: Named number
summary: A whole number that the list stored for this entry under the given name.
details: Vanilla asks for opinion_of_liege in the potential faction members list. Which names exist depends on the list that built the entry. One window passes an empty name, and what that gives is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the stored value.

label: Intrigue skill
summary: Going by its name, the intrigue skill of the entry's character.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it. A neighbouring function, GetMartialSkill, is used with a frame (picture state), so these likely give a skill item rather than a plain number.

label: Learning skill
summary: Going by its name, the learning skill of the entry's character.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it. A neighbouring function, GetMartialSkill, is used with a frame (picture state), so these likely give a skill item rather than a plain number.

label: Martial skill
summary: The martial skill of the entry's character, as an item that has a picture frame.
details: Vanilla reads its frame (picture state) in the army commander selection window. The result is not documented as a plain number.

label: Military strength
summary: A whole number: the military strength of the entry's character.
details: Vanilla shows it with a soldier icon in the situation window, and checks it is above 0 in the dynastic cycle window.

label: Military strength tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the entry's military strength.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the strength number in the dynastic cycle window and in shared list templates.

label: Non-fitting traits count
summary: A whole number: going by its name, how many traits do not fit for the given purpose.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more about its argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; by the name, what the traits should fit.

label: Non-fitting traits text
summary: A text that, going by its name, describes the traits that do not fit.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more about its argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; by the name, what the traits should fit.

label: Opinion of other character
summary: Going by its name, a whole number for the opinion between the entry's character and the other character the list compares with.
details: Vanilla shows it with a sign in the faction window, in a text labelled opinion of the target. Which side holds the opinion and who the other character is depends on the list; the game does not say.

label: Opinion text
summary: Going by its name, a text explaining the opinion of the other character.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more. GetOpinionOfOtherCharacter gives the number.

label: Order index
summary: Going by its name, a whole number giving the entry's place in the order of the list.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Other character items
summary: The list of the other characters' entries that belong to this entry.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in the marriage window. Going by the name and that single use.

label: Prowess skill
summary: Going by its name, the prowess skill of the entry's character.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it. A neighbouring function, GetMartialSkill, is used with a frame (picture state), so these likely give a skill item rather than a plain number.

label: Skill items
summary: The list of skill entries of the entry's character.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in the tax collector, court position and potential scheme agent windows.

label: Stewardship skill
summary: Going by its name, the stewardship skill of the entry's character.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it. A neighbouring function, GetMartialSkill, is used with a frame (picture state), so these likely give a skill item rather than a plain number.

label: Named text
summary: A text that the list stored for this entry under the given name.
details: Vanilla asks for aptitude_label and loyalty_label in the diarchy window. Which names exist depends on the list that built the entry.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the stored text.

label: Title count
summary: A whole number: how many title entries belong to this list entry.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the migration and travel planner windows.

label: Title items
summary: The list of title entries that belong to this list entry.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list, for example in the create-claimant-faction window.

label: Traits
summary: The list of the traits of the entry's character.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of trait lists, and counts it (fewer than 7) in the marriage window.

label: Unselectable reason
summary: The text that says why the entry cannot be selected.
details: Vanilla shows it as a tooltip in the multiplayer lobby and the faith window. IsSelectable tells whether it can be.

label: Has even order index
summary: Going by its name, whether the entry's order number is even.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Has non-fitting traits
summary: Whether, going by its name, the entry's character has traits that do not fit.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more about its argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; by the name, what the traits should fit.

label: Has opinion character
summary: Going by its name, whether the entry has another character to give an opinion of.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it. See GetOpinionOfOtherCharacter.

label: Has other character items
summary: Going by its name, whether the entry has any other character entries.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it. GetOtherCharacterItems gives the list itself.

label: Has titles
summary: Whether the entry has any title entries.
details: Vanilla uses it in shared list templates to show the title part only when there is something to show.

label: Is selectable
summary: Whether the entry can be selected.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the entry in the multiplayer lobby, and in a tooltip adds an error line when it is false.

label: Title list text
summary: A text listing the titles that belong to this entry.
details: Vanilla puts it into the tooltip about the claims the character has, under the line Has claims on the following titles.

label: Entry click
summary: Runs the click action of the list entry, with a name saying what was clicked.
details: Vanilla runs it from clicks on entries in the create-claimant-faction window, with the name 'character'. What other names do depends on the list.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A name for what was clicked.

label: Self
summary: This list entry itself, handed to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to functions that compute data per entry, such as a candidate score or taxable income.

label: Access self
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the sort item itself.
details: No line uses it for this type, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Sort name
summary: The name of a sort option of a character list.
details: Vanilla shows it as a text in the ledger window and in shared list templates.

label: Self
summary: The sort item itself, as a value that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' Self is passed as an argument in the game's texts; no line uses this one.

label: Access self
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the memory itself.
details: No line uses it for this type, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Custom text
summary: A text from a custom localization, evaluated for the memory.
details: The game does not document it. Going by lines where the same function name follows a character, the argument names a custom localization; those lines are only a hint.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; by the hint lines, the name of a custom localization.

label: Creation date
summary: The date the memory was made.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the memories window, and in the copy text of an entry, in front of the description.

label: Memory description
summary: The description text of the memory.
details: Vanilla shows it, capitalized, as the memory's entry in the memories window and its copy text.

label: End date
summary: Going by its name, the date the memory ends.
details: No line uses it for this type. A war results text uses an end date of its own, which is only a hint. HasDuration probably tells whether a memory has one.

label: Memory name
summary: The name of the memory.
details: Vanilla shows it, capitalized, as the tooltip of a memory in the memories window.

label: Memory owner
summary: Going by its name, the character who owns the memory.
details: No line uses it for this type. Other types have a GetOwner of their own, which is only a hint.

label: Description, second person
summary: The memory's description, going by its name written to address the character directly (second person).
details: No line uses it for this type; the hint line shows the name next to character texts in an event. GetThirdPerspectiveDescription is the third-person counterpart.

label: Description, third person
summary: The memory's description told about the character from outside (third person).
details: Vanilla uses it in a legend chapter text, where the protagonist is spoken of as he or she. The perspective is read from the name and that text.

label: Memory type
summary: The type of the memory.
details: Vanilla reads the icon from it, to show a picture of the type in the memories window.

label: Has duration
summary: Going by its name, whether the memory lasts only for a time.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Make script scope
summary: Turns the memory into a script object that other game functions can work with.
details: Vanilla passes it to the function that opens a watch window on a memory when it is clicked. The wording of what the scope allows is inferred from that use.

label: Self
summary: The memory itself, as a value that can be handed to other functions.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' Self is passed as an argument in the game's texts; no line uses this one.

label: Access self
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the memory type itself.
details: No line uses it for this type, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Memory type icon
summary: The icon of the memory type.
details: Vanilla uses it chained from a memory's type as the texture of the memory in the memories window.

label: Memory type name
summary: The name of the memory type.
details: It takes one argument that the game does not describe. No line uses it for this type; the name function exists on many types.

label: Has category
summary: Going by its name, whether the memory type belongs to the given category.
details: No game text or GUI file uses it, and the game documents nothing more about its argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; by the name, the category to check.

label: Self

details: Vanilla runs it from a button of the debug window for watching the character pool.
